slides.headline: is *jan 1* really a cosmic reset?
slides.dek: the calendar flips at midnight. the sky has its own schedule

slides.headline: “the universe resets on january 1st”
slides.body: january 1 is a calendar choice, not a sky event. nothing special happens up there at midnight. but the sky does offer a fresh start soon: the first new moon of 2027 is jan 7, in capricorn.

slides.headline: right now the *moon* is waning, not new
slides.body: it hit last quarter in libra on dec 30, half-lit and shrinking. it reaches new moon on jan 7. on jan 1 the sun meets mercury in capricorn, which is the closest thing to a sky event on new year's day.

slides.headline: astrologers save *beginnings* for new moons
slides.body: a waning moon reads as a time to finish and let go. so the honest astrology of new year's eve is: close things now, start them on jan 7. many also treat the aries equinox in march as the zodiac's new year.

slides.headline: resolutions are fine. a *new deal* is better
slides.body: there is always an 11:11. it does not have to be midnight.
